subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced final-reply `MEDIA:` tokens stay non-delivered with a delivery-boundary warning, or should OpenClaw extract standalone valid `MEDIA:` tokens from code fences?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported user problem is silent media loss; extraction could mutate legitimate code examples, while warn-only preserves delivery behavior and only adds diagnostics.

options.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
options.body: Review and repair the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80396 shape so fenced tokens remain visible text but emit a warning when skipped at delivery.

options.title: Extract fenced standalone tokens
options.body: Change the parser contract to deliver valid standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines, accepting the risk that code examples can become attachments.

options.title: Document as by design
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs to teach plain-text legacy `MEDIA:` formatting, leaving no runtime diagnostic unless a separate warning path is later added.

recommendation.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
recommendation.body: Review and repair the https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80396 shape so fenced tokens remain visible text but emit a warning when skipped at delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the most recent parser/test snapshots and the live candidate PR review state for this exact behavior.
